chunks: Zur‘ah narrated from Samā‘ah, who said:

I asked him about selling fruit, whether it is valid to buy it before its spathe appears. He said: "No, unless he buys with it something else besides it, such as fresh produce or vegetables, and says: I buy from you this fresh produce, this date-palm, and this tree for such-and-such. If the fruit does not emerge, the buyer's capital will be in the fresh produce and vegetables."

He said: And I asked him about the leaves of trees, whether it is valid to buy them for three or four pickings. He said: "If you see the leaves on a tree, then buy from it whatever number of pickings you wish."

key_terms.بَقْلَةً: vegetable or herb included in the transaction
key_terms.رَأْسُ مَالِ الْمُشْتَرِي: the buyer’s principal capital in the sale
key_terms.رَطْبَةً: fresh produce sold together with the uncertain item
key_terms.طَلْعُهَا: its initial visible emergence or spathe

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh to buy fruit before it appears on the tree?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on purchasing fruit before its visible emergence and permits it only when joined with another tangible item such as fresh produce or vegetables. It also permits purchasing tree leaves for multiple pickings once the leaves are visibly present on the tree, showing the importance of reducing uncertainty in sales.
